notesForTheArchitect: Fast-follow unchanged across five rounds and still on the body's line: folding rememberWait's positional arm bool, and renaming readyChecks, which reads no check. The round-two reviewer judged neither a correctness risk.

Two things for the retro learning beyond the four shapes already named. First, round four's red: pi-legion is outside main's required set, so the daemon's checks-red scheduling never fires on it and this change deliberately removes READY's own read of the head's checks - a red lane the base does not require now reaches the merge unless a person or the testing phase reads it. That is the design working as specified and the first live demonstration of what it costs. Second, the technique that made the daemon half drivable in a pod with no Postgres: an outbox built with its pool pointed at a port nothing listens on makes rememberWait self-reporting, returning nil when the gate refused to spend the notice and an error naming the row when it set out to write.
